results.quote: Six chambers: 1 at the head, 6 at the tail.
Nutrient mass is whole units; any split rounds down. (non-negativity not stated)
Chamber limits, 1 to 6: 10, 8, 12, 6, 9, 7.
Pupation marks: 7, 6, 9, 5, 7, 5.
Fallback marks: 3, 2, 4, 2, 3, 2.
Starting mass: 3, 6, 6, 2, 2, 1. Every chamber starts LARVAL.
Above 38, every chamber halves ... Keep one loss tally: tail overflow, burn-off, chamber 1's reabsorbed half, moult sheddings. (the tally's starting value of 0 is not stated)
Finish each job along the whole line before the next:
1. Feed. Add the cycle's ration: ... No trimming yet.
Walk from 1 to 6. Anything above a chamber's limit moves into the next chamber
so overflow can cascade down the line.
Chamber 6's overflow is discarded. ... Keep one loss tally: tail overflow,
A LARVAL chamber at or above its pupation mark goes PUPAL.
A PUPAL chamber at or below its fallback mark goes back to LARVAL
Anything in between holds its stage. Log every change as (cycle, chamber, before, after).
Weigh all six first, then act.
LARVAL chambers burn off a quarter of their mass. ... Keep one loss tally: ... burn-off
PUPAL chambers reabsorb half back into the chamber ahead (one number lower); chamber 1's half is discarded.
No trimming: a chamber can stay over limit until next cycle's overflow, or for good after cycle 5.
Total the line. Above 38, every chamber halves and the shed mass is discarded. At 38 or under, leave it.
Above 38, every chamber halves and the shed mass is discarded. ... moult sheddings. ... the cycles in which a moult fired

mass in chambers 1 to 6, in order; the stage of each chamber (LARVAL or PUPAL); every stage change as (cycle, chamber, before, after); the cycles in which a moult fired; the loss tally; and a balance line: mass at start plus all feed, against mass in the chambers plus the tally.
